doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

title: New CDs, Latin repertoire with Paquito, and goodbye
summary: She describes two unreleased CDs, including a world Latin album with Paquito, Negro and guitarist Farid Haque, thanks Bob Carsey, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well I wish you a lot of luck in your travels.
And I hope you keep writing, you have a very distinctive sound to your work.

Oh thank you, thanks. Well I have two new CDs, they’re not out yet, and they both have new compositions on them. One I recorded live at the Jazz Standard that was with Negro, my regular drummer and Ira Coleman and Ravi Coltrane. And then I did a CD that was very interesting, Latin American music but world Latin American. Like some from Spain, some from Cuba, from Chile, from Brazil, from all over, and that’s like featuring Paquito as one of the guests on there and Farid Haque is playing guitar, with Negro once again and Sante Dibriano is on bass. So we’re doing all these different tunes, and some of them were difficult for me, just to transcribe, to give them, like to transcribe for guitar, for piano, and to get that to sound right. But I did do some originals on all of these.
Is the Latin music of so many different places rhythmically, it’s all a little different, isn’t it?
It must take some study and absorbing before you can play.

I can hear a lot further than what I can play. But Negro was so perfect. He can do anything I write, anything I do, he’s just right there. Just right on it. So it was a lot of fun. And those should come out this year so I’m looking forward to that. It would be fun to tour doing some of that music. And Paquito knew everything. These tunes that I thought

were really, I mean I went to Hawaii and they had this one tune. Nobody would know that, no piano anywhere near that with a singer. And he says, “Oh that’s — I know that, yeah.” And he started playing. He knew every tune I had on the album. Nobody knows all of it. But Bob Carsey was responsible for getting this music to me. You know, “Joanne, I think, listen to this one,” you know, he gave me a whole album to listen to. Some Piazzola, all different things.
Now there’s a name that seems to be on the hot list these days.
Oh boy, yeah. So he came up with these great tunes. So that was a learning experience for me.
Well it’s been a pleasure to meet you. And I wish you the best.
Thank you. It’s been great being here and I’m glad to be a part of your series.
